solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A month to finish new painting around church structure

indicators.note: to finish places the month at the end of the answer
around tells us to turn the new-painting pair back to front

parts.note: art is painting in general
Sept is the short form of September

explanation.surface: An artist must finish a fresh canvas for a church within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal, signalled by 'around', turns the whole new-painting pair, making TRAN; the month is written last despite leading the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the crosswise arm of a cross-shaped church building.

clue.text: Local function entertaining upstanding clergyman

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the function wraps the clergyman

parts.note: tan is tangent, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A local function plays host to an upright vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub; 'upstanding' turns REV into VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or pub, which the British call their local.

clue.text: Like to go round lake, excellent wine-making region

indicators.note: to go round says the like word encloses the lake

parts.note: as means like
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A lake trip around an excellent wine area.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace in north-east France is famous for its Riesling and Gewurztraminer vineyards.

clue.text: Institute invested in sculpture of cow and sheep for main exhibit

indicators.note: invested in means placed within, so the institute letter goes inside
a sculpture shapes material anew, so the farm animals' letters are remodelled

explanation.surface: An institute puts money into a cow-and-sheep sculpture as its star exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests money but means placed inside; the jumble from 'sculpture of' is SHOWPECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is the finest item displayed, the centrepiece of an exhibition.

clue.text: Going by goat, say, giving burden to another

parts.note: passing means going by
a male goat is called a buck, with the article

explanation.surface: A goat walks past someone shifting a load onto somebody else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shifting responsibility onto someone else instead of taking it yourself.

clue.text: Rather soft bananas with yellow filling

indicators.note: filling puts the yellow colour inside the jumbled letters
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of soft go wild

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Soft bananas with a yellow filling sound like a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' reads as fruit but signals a jumble, giving STOF; heraldic gold supplies the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means somewhat or to a degree, a casual synonym of rather.

clue.text: Start working with firm

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
set means firm or solid

explanation.surface: Someone begins a job with a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it means solid.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset is the beginning of something, especially an illness or season.

clue.text: Thin material put on crack is cosmetic, maybe

indicators.note: put on places the fabric before the attempt in a down clue

parts.note: toile is a thin linen or cotton fabric
a crack is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A thin sheet over a crack is a sort of cosmetic fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' means a go at something, not a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic is one example of a toiletry, a product used in washing and grooming.

clue.text: African city's topless event beset by display of disapproval

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the frown encloses the event

parts.note: a frown shows disapproval

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the event word

parts.note: a meet is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A topless event in an African city is met with frowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity but just drops a first letter, leaving EET.
explanation.definitionFit: Freetown is the capital and chief port of Sierra Leone in West Africa.

clue.text: Those who serve exotic Spanish toast aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: exotic signals an unusual reworking of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Waiters serve unusual Spanish toast on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' yields HOPASSISTANT, which splits the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail staff serve customers in a store, so they are those who serve.

clue.text: Pasty noblemen shunning National Trust

indicators.note: shunning says the noblemen avoid the trust, so its letters drop out

parts.note: viscounts are noblemen ranking below earls
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Pale aristocrats steer clear of the National Trust, the British charity that runs stately homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like pale here, but it means thick and sticky like paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pasty has the consistency of paste, that is thick and gluey.

clue.text: Repellent drunk in tube's unfriendly

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the tube

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube

indicators.note: repellent means driving back, so the drunk word is turned round

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: An insect repellent or a drunk in a tube train makes for an unfriendly scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' looks like the definition, but read as driving back it reverses the drunk word into TIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and unfriendly are synonyms describing antagonistic behaviour.

clue.text: Briefly summarise informal talk about international body

indicators.note: about puts the talk around the body

parts.note: rap is an informal chat
EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sum up an informal chat about a global organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to restate the main points briefly, an abbreviation of recapitulate.

clue.text: Restless, as one waiting for doctor might describe himself

definitions.meaning: restless means unable to wait calmly

definitions.text: as one waiting for doctor might describe himself
definitions.meaning: a hospital patient would say ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: A restless patient in the waiting room jokes about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and eager is a synonym sense; split, the word is a patient's self-description.

clue.text: Bird moves gradually and quietly in London borough

indicators.note: in places the moving pieces inside the borough

parts.note: Harrow is a borough of north-west London
edges means inches along
p is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A bird creeps silently through a London neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock, a small brown British songbird, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Mythical king's frolic with maiden penned by unknown author

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the anonymous author wraps the pieces

parts.note: anon is anonymous, an unknown author
a game is a frolic or bit of fun
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A mythic king's romp with a young woman was written by an anonymous author.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the Greek king of Mycenae who led the Trojan War in legend.

clue.text: Charges bungling nutters with abduction of son

indicators.note: abduction of means taking someone in, so the son letter is held inside
bungling means making a mess of, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Charges are laid against crazy people who bungled kidnapping a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungling' gives ENTRUTS. 'Charges' is a verb here, not accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges as a verb means assigns a duty to, the same as gives into someone's care.

clue.text: Imprisoned by monarch, North American soldier once called Ford, among others

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside the monarch

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen
a GI is a US soldier
nee means formerly named

explanation.surface: A North American soldier once called Ford is jailed by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like a soldier's name, but it is Henry Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford was a mechanical engineer, so he is one example of the profession.

clue.text: Innocent remix covering Hotel California is basic

indicators.note: covering means the jumbled letters wrap around the hotel letter
a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters of innocent are reordered

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A remix of the Eagles song Hotel California is called basic and innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remix' yields NONTECNI; the song title is not one unit but two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nontechnical is plain and accessible to a layperson, so elementary or basic.

clue.text: Energy, harnessing river flow

indicators.note: harnessing means holding in, so the energy surrounds the river

parts.note: steam is a source of energy

explanation.surface: Harnessing a river's flow generates energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stream is to flow steadily in a current, a synonym of flow.

clue.text: Boards tailless jet with case of kiwis

indicators.note: tailless removes the final letter of the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: case of takes the outer letters of kiwis

explanation.surface: Kiwis, New Zealanders, board a jet with a damaged tail and their luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Planks are long flat pieces of timber, the same as boards.

clue.text: Curb addiction and return to occupation

parts.note: a rein is a check or curb
a habit is an addiction

explanation.surface: Curbing an addiction helps someone go back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' looks like a job, but here it means living in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinhabit a place is to come back and live in it again.

clue.text: Double-length, sacred plant

indicators.note: double says the letter for length appears twice

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: A sacred plant grows to twice its length.
explanation.walkthrough: The L already in HOLY is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly is an evergreen shrub with spiky leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Glorify sample of Artex to librarian

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone offers a librarian a sample of Artex, a textured ceiling coating, to praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Artex is also the setter's name, a self-referential nod.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, a synonym of glorify.

clue.text: Finish casing air-conditioning

parts.note: a shell is an outer casing

explanation.surface: A builder completes the housing for an air-conditioning unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' is a noun: a varnish coat, not the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish used as a glossy surface coating on wood.

clue.text: Older relative eager for fabric

parts.note: nan is a grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Grandma is keen to get her hands on some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing in China.

clue.text: Bouquets received after reports about promotion

indicators.note: about puts the reports around the promotion

parts.note: says means reports or states
PR is public relations, promotional work

explanation.surface: Flowers arrive after news of someone's promotion at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprays are small bunches of flowers, a type of bouquet.

clue.text: First of trilogy by star author delivers tragic events

indicators.note: First of takes the opening letter of trilogy

parts.note: the sun is a star
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

explanation.surface: The first book of a trilogy by a star author delivers tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves causing catastrophic disasters on coasts.
